primary_diagnosis: Cholelithiasis (Gallbladder Stones) with Chronic Functional Constipation
secondary_diagnoses: Menorrhagia (heavy menstrual bleeding — resolved / under observation)
clinical_reasoning: Patient is an elderly female with USG-confirmed gallbladder stone (cholelithiasis) discovered during investigation of menorrhagia. The stone was deemed non-surgical at AIIMS due to absence of acute pain. Current symptoms are severe constipation (stool only every 2-3 days) and gas, classic manifestations of impaired biliary digestion and altered bowel motility. Pre-existing rheumatoid arthritis medication (e.g. NSAIDs/DMARDs) may further contribute to constipation. The triad of gallstones, chronic constipation, and flatulence points toward biliary-associated gastrointestinal dysmotility.
recommended_tests: Repeat Abdominal USG to assess gallstone status and biliary duct caliber
Liver Function Tests (LFT) including Bilirubin, ALP, and GGT
Thyroid Function Tests (TSH, FT4) to rule out secondary hypothyroidism
Complete Blood Count (CBC) to screen for occult anemia
